KR.read: Korea's deodorants segment now has data, though the size read is dated: a MEDIUM-confidence Euromonitor-via-Pharm-News figure puts the domestic RETAIL market at KRW 63.7bn in 2018 (~US$43.1mn), the most recent Korean-language figure that could be verified on a fetched page. A separate LOW-confidence figure from Actual Market Research states the market was 'more than' US$160mn in 2023 - a floor, not a point estimate, and roughly 3.7x the 2018 figure on a USD basis with no stated definitional change, so the two should not be averaged. A HIGH-confidence Euromonitor figure also shows the category is highly concentrated: Beiersdorf Korea (Nivea) holds a 'commanding' 59% share in 2025, though the underlying value figures behind that share are paywalled.
KR.trend: The only growth figure is also 2018-vintage: +7.0% (MEDIUM confidence, Euromonitor-via-Pharm-News, domestic RETAIL, KRW terms). No forecast CAGR could be found on any fetchable page for this segment - a Statista Consumer Market Outlook page and a Sphericalinsights page were checked but returned unusable (paywalled/unreachable) content, so this remains an open research gap.
KR.caveats: The only sourced size and growth figures for this segment are both 2018-vintage; treat the market as stale-dated rather than current. The 2023 Actual Market Research figure is stated as a floor ('more than US$160mn') and its scope may include antiperspirant/body-mist adjacencies not covered by the 2018 figure, so the two should not be read as a continuous series. cagr_forecast remains a standing gap for Korea.

IN.read: India's deodorants segment now has a RETAIL size read: US$1.0bn (2025, LOW confidence, IMARC Group, rounded to one decimal by the source). A MEDIUM-confidence company proxy also exists: Vini Cosmetics (maker of Fogg, India's largest deodorant brand by volume share) reported revenue growth of 17% for the year ending March 2025 (FY25, NET_REALISATION basis, sourced from Tracxn's MCA/ROC-filing-based profile) - a company figure, not a category-wide market growth rate, used because no brand-level or category-wide growth figure could be found for the larger diversified players (HUL, Godrej, ITC) where deodorants is one line among many. A similarly-sourced proxy for McNroe Consumer Products (Wild Stone, the #2 deodorant maker) shows a directionally consistent 20% figure for the same period, though this is noted for context rather than recorded as an independent claim.
IN.trend: Three forecast CAGRs exist on essentially the same product scope (sprays, roll-ons, creams, gels, sticks, wipes) and span a wide 3.10-9.13% range: IMARC 3.10% (2026-2034, LOW), Expert Market Research 7.80% (2026-2035, LOW), and Bonafide Research 9.13% (2024-2029, LOW) - a roughly 3x spread between the extremes that the sources do not reconcile. The Vini Cosmetics 17% figure is the only observed year-on-year read, and it is company-level, not a category rate.
IN.caveats: The three forecast CAGRs disagree by up to 3x on effectively the same scope and should not be averaged. The Vini Cosmetics growth figure is a single company (India's #1 deodorant brand by volume) standing in for the category because no category-wide or diversified-player figure could be sourced; organised-market only, with no unorganised-market read implied. Organised-vs-unorganised coverage is not stated by any of the three forecast sources.

combined.read: Both geographies now carry a RETAIL market-size figure, but neither is on solid footing for a direct comparison: Korea's is 2018-vintage (KRW 63.7bn, ~US$43.1mn) alongside a 2023 floor-only figure (>US$160mn) that may cover a different scope, while India's (US$1.0bn, 2025) is a single current-year LOW-confidence read. Given Korea's most defensible figure is seven years stale, a same-period KR-vs-IN size comparison is not attempted here. No [CORRIDOR]-tagged data point exists for deodorants in either file, and deodorants is not among the segments flagged as corridor-relevant in config/corridor.yaml.
